WhatItMeans: Life pays you back in kind — the harm or good you send out will come back to you, sooner or later, as surely as a circle closing.
WhatTheBibleSays: The Bible does teach that actions have consequences: "whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap" (Galatians 6:7), and Proverbs 26:27 says whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein. But the Bible's version is God's justice, not automatic karma — consequences come from the Lord's hand, in His time, and sometimes grace interrupts the circle entirely, as it did for the thief on the cross. I believe the principle behind the saying is biblical, while the saying itself turns God's personal justice into an impersonal law of payback, and that is not the same thing.
Origin: A modern American proverb, first documented in print in 1974 in Eddie Stone's book Donald Writes No More; linguists trace it to an African proverb that entered general use through African-American speech. It was popularised in song — by The Stylistics, and later by Justin Timberlake's 2006 hit. The underlying idea is ancient, but the wording is twentieth-century.
Sources: Eddie Stone, Donald Writes No More (1974); on-site KJV text of Galatians 6:7 and Proverbs 26:27
